statements.paraphrase: NCCIH states that ashwagandha should be avoided during pregnancy.
statements.quote: Ashwagandha should be avoided during pregnancy.
statements.scope: Ashwagandha generally (supplements/preparations). Page gives no mechanism or study detail for this statement.

statements.paraphrase: NCCIH states that ashwagandha should not be used while breastfeeding.
statements.quote: should not be used while breastfeeding.
statements.scope: Ashwagandha generally. No further detail given on the page.

statements.paraphrase: NCCIH notes rare reported cases linking liver injury to ashwagandha supplements.
statements.scope: Supplements; described as rare case reports, not an established incidence.

statements.paraphrase: NCCIH says ashwagandha is not recommended for people about to have surgery or with autoimmune or thyroid disorders.
NCCIH says people with hormone-sensitive prostate cancer should avoid it because it may increase testosterone levels.
NCCIH says there is evidence ashwagandha might interact with some medications, naming diabetes, blood-pressure, immunosuppressant, sedative, anti-seizure and thyroid-hormone medicines.
statements.scope: Named medication classes only; this is not an assessment of any specific drug the user lists.

statements.paraphrase: NCCIH says it may be safe short-term (up to 3 months) and that long-term safety cannot be concluded from available information; some people may have drowsiness, stomach upset, diarrhoea or vomiting.
statements.scope: General population statement; not a clearance for any individual.
